# rlsbl options

Print rlsbl's options registry, and write this repository's entries for rlsbl's options in .strictmetadata/options/ at its git root. Every rlsbl check is an option, rlsbl:<check name>, ranked error > warn > off for an error check and warn > off for a warning check, and a few options are not checks; `rlsbl options registry` lists every one. `rlsbl check` and every release apply each entry's current value (off: the check does not run; warn: it runs and reports, never blocking; error: as registered). The options representing an adoption default to off and accept a path scope naming one workspace member. Invalid entries stop every check run and every release.

## options registry

Print rlsbl's options registry: one option per check, rlsbl:<check name>, plus the options that are not checks, each with the subject file its entries are filed under, the values it ranks strongest first, its default, its scope type, the options it requires, and what it governs. The TOML printed is the registry document rlsbl ships, in the shape of strictspec's built-in options-registry schema; with --json the same declarations are the payload. Needs no rlsbl project.

**Effect:** read_only

## options set

Write one rlsbl entry into .strictmetadata/options/<subject>.toml at the repository's git root, or update the entry already there for the same option and scope, keeping every other line of the document. The subject file is the one the option's registry declaration names. Creates .strictmetadata/options/ and its manifest.toml, naming strictspec as the owner, when absent. strictspec validates the result before anything is written (every document's shape, and every rlsbl entry with this one in place), and each refusal is its catalogued diagnostic: an unknown option, a value the option does not declare, a current ranked above the ideal, an entry equal to the default, an empty reason, an option switched off while an option requiring it is not. A --scope must name a workspace member's path as .strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml declares it, and only the options declaring the path scope type accept one. Refuses an id outside the rlsbl namespace and a manifest naming another owner. The written files are committed with the Autogenerated trailer unless --no-auto-commit is passed.

**Effect:** mutating

### Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--current` |  | str | required |  | The value the repository runs the option at now: error, warn, or off for an error check; warn or off for a warning check; the values `rlsbl options registry` lists for any other option |
| `--ideal` |  | str | required |  | The value the repository should run the option at: one the option declares, never ranked below current, or non-existent when the right value is one rlsbl does not offer yet |
| `--reason` |  | str | required |  | Why the repository deviates from the option's default, in one sentence, recorded in the entry as written |
| `--scope` |  | str | optional |  | Narrow the entry to one workspace member, named by its path (packages/widget, say); accepted only by the options declaring the path scope type. Without it the entry covers the whole repository |
| `--auto-commit`, `--no-auto-commit` |  | bool | optional |  | Commit the written files with the Autogenerated trailer (committed when neither --auto-commit nor --no-auto-commit is passed) |

### Arguments

| Name | Type | Presence | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | str | required | The option, as rlsbl:<name> (rlsbl:dep-floors, say); `rlsbl options registry` names every option |
